items.title: Section: Patience's Four Powers — The Turtle Who Couldn't Stay Silent, and Rāhula's Two Lessons

items.zh: 忍辱四相者，謂諸菩薩修行忍辱，能斷不忍，忍所對治。是名第一。即此忍辱，能作自己菩提資糧，亦即能作同事攝事成熟有情。是名第二。由此忍辱，濟㧋自他大怖畏事，饒益自他。
items.en: Patience's four aspects: bodhisattvas who practice patience are able to break intolerance, the very thing patience directly opposes. ... Through this patience, they rescue both self and others from great fearful matters, benefiting both.

items.zh: 是名第三。
由是因緣，能令菩薩於當來世無多怨敵、無多離隔、無多憂苦；於現法中，臨命終時心無憂悔，身壞已後生於善趣天世界中。
items.en: By this cause, bodhisattvas come to have few enemies in future lives, few who would estrange them from friends, and little grief; in this very life, at the time of death their mind holds no regret, and once the body has perished they are reborn among the heavens, a favourable realm.

items.zh: 是名第四。是名忍辱威力四相。此外無有若過若增。

items.title: Section: Diligence's Four Powers, and the Bee Who Kept a Sleepy Monk Awake

items.zh: 精進四相者，謂諸菩薩住勤精進，能斷懈怠，精進所治。是名第一。即此精進，能作自己菩提資糧及所依止，亦即能作同事攝事成熟有情。是名第二。勤精進故，得安樂住。不為一切惡不善法之所雜亂，後後所證轉勝於前，倍生歡喜，以自饒益；勤修善品，不以身語損惱於他，令他發生精進樂欲，以饒益他。
items.en: Diligence's four aspects: bodhisattvas abiding in diligent effort are able to break laziness, the very thing diligence directly opposes. ... Through diligent effort, they attain a joyful abiding undisturbed by any unwholesome state, each attainment surpassing the one before it, redoubling their own joy, benefiting themselves; diligently cultivating wholesome practices, they never harm others through body or speech, and inspire in others the same joyful wish for diligence, benefiting others.

items.zh: 是名第三。
由此因力，於當來世，愛樂殊勝士夫功業。是名第四。
items.en: By the power of this cause, in future lives they come to genuinely admire the difficult, extraordinary achievements of truly excellent beings. This is the fourth.

items.zh: 是名精進威力四相。此外無有若過若增。

items.title: Section: Concentration's Four Powers, and the Turtle That Outwitted a Hungry Otter

items.zh: 靜慮四相者，謂諸菩薩入靜慮時，能斷煩惱、語言尋、伺、喜、樂、色想等隨煩惱，靜慮所治。是名第一。
items.en: Concentration's four aspects: bodhisattvas, upon entering concentration, are able to break the afflictions, the discursive deliberation that produces speech, and the secondary hindrances of joy, pleasure, and fixation on form — all of which concentration directly opposes. This is the first.

items.zh: 即此靜慮，能作自己菩提資糧及所依止，亦即能作同事攝事成熟有情。是名第二。
現法樂住以自饒益，其心寂靜、最極寂靜，遠離貪愛；於諸有情無損、無惱，以饒益他。是名第三。由此因緣，智得清淨，能發神通，於當來世生淨天處，得靜慮果。
items.en: Abiding in present ease benefits themselves — the mind grows still, then utterly still, released from craving; and causing no harm or disturbance to any being benefits others. ... By this cause, wisdom becomes purified, miraculous ability is unlocked, and in future lives they are reborn among the pure heavens, the very fruit of concentration.

items.zh: 是名第四。是名靜慮威力四相。此外無有若過若增。

items.title: Wisdom's Four Powers Complete All Six Perfections, Closing the Dharma's Power in Full

items.zh: 般若四相者，謂諸菩薩具足妙慧，能斷無明，慧所對治。是名第一。即此般若，能作自己菩提資糧，能以布施、愛語、利行、同事攝事成熟有情。是名第二。於所知事如義覺了，能引廣大清淨歡喜，以自饒益；普為有情稱理說法，令其獲得現法當來利益安樂，以饒益他。
items.en: Wisdom's four aspects: bodhisattvas endowed with wondrous wisdom are able to break ignorance, the very thing wisdom directly opposes. ... Comprehending the object of knowledge exactly as it truly is, they bring forth vast and pure joy, benefiting themselves; and teaching every being the Dharma in accordance with genuine principle, they grant them benefit and ease both now and in the future, benefiting others.

items.zh: 是名第三。
由是因緣，攝諸善根，能正所作，於當來世能證二障離繫，謂煩惱障離繫及所知障離繫。是名第四。是名般若威力四相。此外無有若過若增。是名法威力。
items.en: By this cause, gathering every wholesome root and rightly accomplishing every task, they come in future lives to be released from both obstructions — release from the afflictive obstruction, and release from the cognitive obstruction. This is the fourth. ... This is called the power of the Dharma.

items.title: Section: Innate Power Opens — Bearing Immense Suffering Without a Second Thought, and Delighting in the Cost of Helping

items.zh: 云何諸佛菩薩俱生威力？謂性能憶念諸本生事。為欲利益諸有情故，不由思擇，於極長時種種猛利無間大苦悉能堪忍。
items.en: What is the innate power of buddhas and bodhisattvas? It is that, by nature, they recollect their own past births, and for the sake of benefiting sentient beings, without needing to deliberate at all, they are able to endure every kind of intense, uninterrupted, and immense suffering across an extremely long span of time.

items.zh: 為欲利益諸有情故，欣樂領受能辦有情利益事苦。
items.en: For the sake of benefiting sentient beings, they joyfully and gladly receive whatever suffering accomplishing genuine benefit for beings requires.

items.title: Section: Born in Tuṣita Heaven — Cosmic Lifespans, and Three Marks That Outshine Every Other God

items.zh: 為欲利益諸有情故，上生第四覩史多天，盡覩史多壽量而住。有三勝事，映彼受生諸天子眾。一、天壽量，二、天形色，三、天名稱。
items.en: For the sake of benefiting sentient beings, they ascend to the fourth heaven, Tuṣita, and dwell there for the entirety of that heaven's lifespan. Three excellent marks outshine every other god born there: first, the fullness of their heavenly lifespan; second, their heavenly form; and third, their heavenly renown.

items.title: Section: A Buddha's Descent to the Human World — Fully Aware Through Birth Itself, Unlike Any Other Being

items.zh: 將欲下生入母胎時，放大光明，普照世界。於降母胎入、住、出位，皆正了知。既出胎已，即於地上，不待扶侍而行七步，自稱德號。
items.en: As they are about to descend and enter the mother's womb, they radiate great light, illuminating the entire world. Throughout entering, dwelling in, and leaving the womb, they remain fully and correctly aware. Once born, standing on the ground, without needing any support, they walk seven steps and proclaim their own excellent title.

items.zh: 於初生時，有大威德天、龍、藥叉、健達縛、阿素洛、揭路荼、緊捺洛、牟呼洛伽等，散以種種天妙華香，持天伎樂、上妙衣服、幢幡、寶蓋，殊勝供具而為供養。又以無上三十二大丈夫相等，莊嚴其身。住最後有最後生中，一切怨敵、一切魔軍、一切災橫不能侵害。坐菩提座，以慈定力摧伏眾魔。一一支節，皆悉備足那羅延力。
items.en: At the moment of birth, mighty gods, nāgas, and yakṣas ... scatter every kind of wondrous heavenly flower and incense, play heavenly music ... and make offerings of every excellent kind. They are further adorned with the unsurpassed thirty-two marks of a great being. ... Every single limb and joint is fully endowed with the strength of Nārāyaṇa.

blocks.text: The power of the remaining perfections, then the "innate power" of a Buddha's life story, told as a list of marvels.

It breaks intolerance; "rescues both self and others from great fearful matters"; leads to "few enemies, few who would estrange them, little grief; at death no regret". Master Cháng Bǎi recalls the Buddha's teaching to Rāhula on patience.
It breaks laziness; brings "a joyful abiding undisturbed by any unwholesome state"; and in future lives one admires "the difficult achievements of truly excellent beings".

It breaks afflictions and the discursive thought, joy, pleasure, and form-perception of the lower levels; "the mind grows still, then utterly still, released from craving"; it "purifies wisdom and unlocks miraculous ability".
It breaks ignorance; "comprehending the object of knowledge as it truly is"; and leads to release "from both obstructions, afflictive and cognitive".

"By nature they recollect their past births", and for beings' sake "endure every kind of intense suffering without needing to deliberate". "They joyfully receive whatever suffering helping beings requires."

They dwell in Tuṣita heaven for its whole lifespan, outshining every god there. Descending, "they radiate great light"; "throughout entering, dwelling in, and leaving the womb, they remain fully aware". Venerable Miào Jìng: because of their merit and wisdom. At birth, gods scatter flowers and play music.

quiz.q: Patience "rescues self and others from fearful matters." After the Rāhula story, what does Master Cháng Bǎi say Rāhula was foremost in?
options: inconspicuous practice — guarding speech and mind, careful of verbal karma
quiz.why: "Through this patience, they rescue both self and others from great fearful matters, benefiting both." Master Cháng Bǎi: hence the scriptures say Rāhula was foremost in inconspicuous practice — always guarding his speech and mind, never speaking carelessly, very careful of verbal karma.

quiz.q: Diligence "breaks laziness." How does Master Cháng Bǎi distinguish 懈怠 and 懶惰?
options: not growing arisen merit is 懈怠; not pursuing unattained merit is 懶惰
quiz.why: "Diligence's four aspects: bodhisattvas abiding in diligent effort are able to break laziness, the very thing diligence directly opposes." Master Cháng Bǎi: not continuing to cultivate and grow merit already arisen is 懈怠; not developing merit not yet attained is 懶惰.

quiz.q: Concentration: "the mind grows still, then utterly still." How does Venerable Miào Jìng distinguish them?
options: free of craving for worldly desire is "still"; free of craving for dhyāna is "utterly still"
quiz.why: "Abiding in present ease benefits themselves — the mind grows still, then utterly still, released from craving." Venerable Miào Jìng: free of craving for worldly desire is "the mind still"; free of craving for dhyāna itself is "utterly still."

quiz.q: Concentration "purifies wisdom and unlocks miraculous ability." What saying does Master Cháng Bǎi cite?
options: "superior powers don't arise without concentration; uncontaminated wisdom doesn't unfold without stillness"
quiz.why: "By this cause, wisdom becomes purified, miraculous ability is unlocked, and in future lives they are reborn among the pure heavens, the very fruit of concentration." Master Cháng Bǎi, citing the Zhū jīng yào jí: "The superior work of powers doesn't arise without concentration; the root of uncontaminated wisdom doesn't unfold without stillness."

quiz.q: Wisdom "breaks ignorance." What two kinds does Master Cháng Bǎi say bodhisattvas cut?
options: the manifest forms of ignorance clinging to self and to phenomena
quiz.why: "Wisdom's four aspects: bodhisattvas endowed with wondrous wisdom are able to break ignorance, the very thing wisdom directly opposes." Master Cháng Bǎi: what bodhisattvas cut are the manifestations of two afflictions — ignorance clinging to self and ignorance clinging to phenomena.

quiz.q: Innate power: "without deliberating, enduring immense suffering over long ages." What does Master Cháng Bǎi say?
options: without special deliberation, guiding beings in this world for vast ages
quiz.why: "For the sake of benefiting sentient beings, without needing to deliberate at all, they are able to endure every kind of intense, uninterrupted, and immense suffering across an extremely long span of time." Master Cháng Bǎi: without special deliberation, guiding beings in the Sahā world for an extremely long time.

quiz.q: "Throughout entering, dwelling in, and leaving the womb, fully aware." Why, per Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: superior merit and wisdom make mindfulness strong — aware throughout
quiz.why: "Throughout entering, dwelling in, and leaving the womb, they remain fully and correctly aware." Venerable Miào Jìng: because his merit and wisdom are both superior, his mindfulness is strong — he knows entering, dwelling, and leaving.
